rationale: NULL pointer dereference. Inherited Linkability from the Pointer Issues category, which it cannot support: a null dereference aborts the process and links no data subjects. The observable effect is a crash that reveals system state, which is Detectability.

Out-of-bounds read. Data Disclosure is direct and correct. Linkability was inherited from Memory Buffer Errors and is second-order at best: it requires the leaked bytes to happen to contain correlatable identifiers, which the CWE does not assert.

Out-of-bounds write. A write primitive corrupts rather than discloses; Data Disclosure is retained because corrupted adjacent memory is commonly read back. Linkability dropped for the same reason as CWE-125.
Use after free. Reads of freed memory expose stale contents, so Data Disclosure holds. Linkability inherited from Memory Buffer Errors and Pointer Issues is unsupported.
Double free. Same reasoning as CWE-416.
Classic buffer copy without size check. Same reasoning as CWE-787.
Path traversal. Reading arbitrary files is squarely Data Disclosure. Linkability inherited from File Handling Issues is not asserted by the weakness itself.
Symlink following. Same reasoning as CWE-22.

OS command injection. Data Disclosure retained. Linkability dropped as unsupported. Note the inherited set is arguably too NARROW rather than too broad here, since arbitrary execution also enables log tampering (Non-repudiation) and covert processing (Unawareness); left out pending evidence rather than asserted.
Memory leak. Resource exhaustion is observable behaviour, not disclosure. Inherited Data Disclosure from Resource Management Errors is unsupported for a leak.

Resource Management Errors used as a bare category tag. Exhaustion is observable; Data Disclosure was inherited from the category-level decision justified by CWE-770, which does not generalise to the category.

Allocation without limits. REVIEWED AND UNCHANGED. CONSTRUCTION.md records this CWE as the deliberate synthetic-example target for Data Disclosure; overriding it would contradict the authored synthetic set. Flagged for your decision rather than changed.
Information exposure. REVIEWED AND UNCHANGED. All three classes are directly supported and this is the canonical privacy CWE.
Cryptographic issues. REVIEWED AND UNCHANGED. Weak crypto undermines all three.

Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File. Inherited Non-repudiation alone from Audit / Logging Errors, which assigns by MECHANISM (logging) and misses the EFFECT the CWE name states outright: sensitive information is exposed. Data Disclosure added; Non-repudiation retained because a log is a genuinely attributable record. Caught by the anchor test, and material - this CWE was 57% of the entire Non-repudiation class.

Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information. Inherited Detectability;Identifiability;Linkability from Cryptographic Issues. Data Disclosure added - readable stored data is the whole weakness. Detectability dropped: it derives from crypto acting as an oracle, which is not the mechanism for plaintext at rest. Caught by the anchor test.

Use of Hard-coded Credentials. Category membership supplied by cwe_category_additions.csv (Authentication Errors), giving Identifiability;Linkability. Data Disclosure added for consistency with CWE-312: an embedded credential is readable by anyone with the source or binary, which is disclosure of a secret.
